What is the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ across the curve $C$ shown above?

*Hint: Start by checking whether $F$ is source-free.*
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2},$ then the following are equivalent:

- $F$ is a source-free vector field.

- $∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.$

- The flux ${∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s$ along any closed curve $C⊂D$ is zero.

- Flux is path-independent. That is, given any two curves ${C}_{1},{C}_{2}⊂D$ with the same start and endpoints, we have that

$$
{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s.
$$

- There exists a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ for $F.$

First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $F$ is *not* a source-free vector field. 

Since $F$ is not source-free, we do not have enough information to determine the flux of $F$ through $C.$
